Department of Health officials were unable to provide key details about the government’s proposed changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) at an inquiry this week.

Amendments before parliament seek to reduce long-term costs by allocating funding based on “functional capacity” rather than diagnoses.

This would act as a de facto means test on the family and community’s capacity to support a scheme’s applicant.

Coupled with explicit cuts to certain kinds of support, it is expected to save more than $36 billion over the next four years, reducing cost growth from 11.6%
